text:
amanda: Heads-up — customer `acme-fin` opened a support ticket: p95 latency jumped ~3.1x after we onboarded nova-extended-v1 yesterday. They see it only on long-context requests (>20k tokens).
kevin: thanks — any repro payload or sample?
amanda: pasted excerpt from their repro (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "nova-extended-v1", 
  "input": "<~20k tokens of log/context>", 
  "max_tokens": 1024
}
```
maria: have we changed tokenizer or bpe merges for nova-extended?
amanda: we did a tokenizer tweak to merge rare-multi-byte sequences to reduce token count overall — landed in the model pack used by hosted. deploy-bot: canary rollout nova-extended-v1 -> 10% hosts @ 1999990500; completed 1999990950 :rocket: 
olga: that would change tokenization boundary counts — could break our KV cache hit rates for long prefixes. If token counts differ, prefix kv keys mismatch and cache fallback to cold path. That would amplify p95.
sahil: checking metrics now — infra-bot: kvcache.hit_rate for nova-extended-v1 longctx requests dropped from 0.72 -> 0.09 around 1999990600.
amanda: that's huge. so it's likely cache churn not model compute? Any CPU/GPU saturation?
kevin: GPU util on hosts serving nova-extended is steady ~64%, but tail latency per-token compute is similar. The tail is from more full-sequence attention paths + cache misses.
maria: can you dump a tokenization example? need to compare old vs new token counts for same input.
amanda: pasted minimal repro diff: 
```
input: "中文字符...<long chunk>"
old_token_count: 18342
new_token_count: 19610
```
olga: +1200 tokens -> more KV entries and different cache keys. Also kvcache page alignment changed — more cache invalidations.
sahil: action plan i) pin affected customers to nova-extended:v0 (previous pack) ii) roll back tokenizer tweak from hosted model pack iii) temporary routing to fallback model variant (nova-compact) for long-context queries.
amanda: acme-fin needs mitigation asap. can we pin them?
kevin: yes — set per-customer routing: `rwctl routing set acme-fin --model=nova-extended:v0.9 --scope=long_context` (example). will do now.
kevin: done. confirmed traffic to acme-fin routed to v0.9 at 1999991102. pinging acme to verify.
amanda: they report improvement, p95 back to baseline within 8m :tada:
maria: good. next: reproduce in dev and write regression test. I want a unit test in tokenizer to assert token count stability for long-biased inputs.
olga: also need kvcache keying to include a tokenizer-version hash so caches don't collide across tokenization changes — otherwise silent correctness/perf blasts. Filing infra ticket.
sahil: opened ticket INFRA-9876: "kv cache: include tokenizer fingerprint in keys". link: https://redwood-internal/INFRA-9876
amanda: for short-term we should: 1) revert tokenizer tweak in hosted packs 2) add rollout freeze for tokenizer-affecting changes 3) add alert on sudden kvcache hit rate drops per model variant
kevin: revert queued, will schedule canary rollback at 1999991400. deploy-bot: rollback pipeline triggered for nova-extended tokenizer-change canary @ 1999991420.
amanda: one more thing — some customers use deduping heuristics that rely on token counts; we should notify accounts who've used long-context on nova-extended in last 30 days. support-bot: broadcast drafted to customer-ops channel.
maria: on repro, here are quick commands we used to compare tokenizers locally: 
```
# python snippet
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
old = Tokenizer.from_file('nova_old.json')
new = Tokenizer.from_file('nova_new.json')
s = open('large_ctx.txt').read()
print(len(old.encode(s).tokens), len(new.encode(s).tokens))
```
olga: also observed increased RPCs between runtime and kvcache-store due to smaller sizes per entry — more roundtrips. will profile.
sahil: longer-term mitigations: - make kv cache resilient to tokenization changes (fingerprint+fallback buckets) - surface tokenizer metadata in model manifest so routing/console can warn - include tokenization diff in model-onboard checklist
amanda: recording thread summary for ticket: root cause = tokenizer BPE tweak changed tokenization boundaries -> increased token counts and key mismatch -> kvcache hit-rate collapse for long-context -> p95 spike. Immediate fix = customer routing pin and revert tokenizer tweak in hosted packs. Next steps = kvcache keying improvement + rollout policy changes + tests.
kevin: closing loop with acme-fin; they requested SLA rebate form; ops to handle.
amanda: nice work — add postmortem if we keep rollback longer than 72h.
infra-bot: note: metric alerts created — kvcache.hit_rate_drop and model.p95_regression correlated.
amanda: thanks all, i'll file support ticket with full timeline and attach logs.
